notes: All candidates, party lines and spellings come from official SOTS town sample ballots (portal.ct.gov) for the Nov 3, 2026 State Election, decoded from PDF with a Python standard-library script. Ballots read: North Branford (CD3), Bloomfield and Torrington (CD1), Norwich (CD2), Westport, Greenwich and Fairfield (CD4), Meriden and Torrington (CD5).

Ballot columns are Democratic (A), Republican (B), Working Families (C), Independent (D); CD1 adds a Green Party column. Fusion lines are combined, major party first; 'Independent' is the Independent Party of Connecticut line, not 'unaffiliated'.
Statewide candidates are identical on every ballot read; no Libertarian or Green statewide candidates appear.
No U.S. Senate race in Connecticut in 2026 (Blumenthal's term runs to 2029, Murphy's to 2031).
CD1: Luke Bronin defeated Rep. John Larson in the Aug 11, 2026 Democratic primary (CT Mirror / CT Public); Larson is not on the ballot. Mark Stewart Greenstein is a write-in, left out.
No statewide question appears on any of the sample ballots read; the only question found (Norwich police headquarters bond) is local and left out.
Polls in Connecticut are open 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM; the whole state is Eastern time, EST (UTC-5) after DST ends Nov 1.
unconfirmed: No official SOTS statement or list of 2026 statewide ballot questions was found; 'no statewide questions' rests on sample ballots from all five districts plus news/Ballotpedia searches (Ballotpedia's CT 2026 measures page could not be read).
The SOTS consolidated statewide candidate list was not found as a readable page; candidates come from town sample ballots, so a late change after those ballots were posted would be missed.
Some sample ballots (Hartford, Bridgeport, Danbury, Avon) use font encodings the decoder could not read; the districts were covered by other towns.
Measure effective date is reference only (no measures); the exact canvass date was not checked.
